PullRequest.Title: agentHost: eagerly load rename_chat for active title generation
PullRequest.Body:

Backport of #340017 to `release/1.141`.

Make `rename_chat` immediately available when active-agent title generation asks the agent to name a new chat. Keep the tool deferred for explicit rename requests under other title-generation strategies.

Validation:
- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run hygiene` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --grep "definitions and confirmation|rename_chat is eager only|deferred naming keeps explicit rename tools"` — 3 passing

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed flag, provider mappings, session-lifetime strategy, and post-rename reminder suppression are directly traced in code. The exact latency varies with provider prompt caching and chat length, which limits severity, but not the repeated eager-schema mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: The roughly 1 KB `rename_chat` description and JSON schema, plus the model's input-token processing for that schema
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For Claude and for Copilot sessions with tool search active, the extra schema cost repeats on every model request for the lifetime of each active-agent session, including restored sessions whose title was already generated; cost grows linearly with subsequent turns and concurrently active sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated model-request bytes and input-token work increase per-turn latency and model/network throughput consumption after automatic naming no longer needs the tool.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: `rename_chat` retained `deferLoading: true`, so supported runtimes kept its full schema out of normal model requests and loaded it through tool discovery only when needed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every session whose immutable title-generation strategy is `activeAgent` now receives `deferLoading: false`, regardless of whether its automatic title is still pending.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added return at line 1857 overrides the base definition's `deferLoading: true` with `false` for all `activeAgent` sessions, introducing unconditional eager loading beyond the initial title-generation turn.
Findings.Title: Defer `rename_chat` again after the title is settled
Findings.Impact: After the first `rename_chat` call, `markTitleRenamed` suppresses the naming reminder, but the session strategy remains `activeAgent`; every later turn—and every restored already-named session—still eagerly sends this tool. Claude maps the flag to `alwaysLoad: true`, and Copilot maps it to `defer: 'never'` when tool search is active, so long chats repeatedly pay for a tool needed only during initial naming.
Findings.Evidence: `prepareInstructionForAgent` stops requesting automatic naming once `_renamedTitles` is set or persisted title source is agent/user (`agentHostSessionTitleController.ts:552-568`), while the strategy is retained for the session. This new branch checks only that strategy. The resulting flag is consumed as `alwaysLoad: !def.deferLoading` by Claude (`claudeServerToolMcpServer.ts:76`) and as `defer: ... ? 'auto' : 'never'` by Copilot (`copilotAgentSession.ts:2983`); both provider tool inventories are built at launch. The definition includes a long description and four-property schema (`sessionServerTools.ts:134-143,228-234`).
Findings.Recommendation: Base eagerness on whether automatic naming is actually pending (including persisted title source), and refresh/rematerialize the provider tool metadata after a successful rename; restored or already-renamed active-agent sessions should keep `rename_chat` deferred.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or first-use a new session with active-agent title generation and send its first substantive prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider startup materializes the session tool inventory before the model turn. The first model request must receive `rename_chat` eagerly so the injected title reminder can be fulfilled; the later automatic rename returns before its existing persistence completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send an eagerly loaded tool description/schema as part of the model-visible tool inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional eager schema for the first model request of each active-agent session on Claude and on Copilot when tool search is active; Codex already treats all dynamic tools as eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The schema remained deferred and supported runtimes required tool discovery before the model could call it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The schema is on the first model request critical path, while making it eager can avoid a prior discovery/tool-search step before the required rename.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist chat and session title metadata after the model invokes `rename_chat`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one automatic naming call for a successfully named fresh chat under the intended flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rename execution and persistence occurred after the deferred tool was discovered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Automatic calls return before this persistence completes, so the database writes are off the model turn's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One `rename_chat` definition per active-agent session; first-turn cost is constant per newly created session, while multiple simultaneously started sessions each carry their own model request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active model turn per chat; separate sessions can start concurrently. The rename persistence path is existing background work and is not made more concurrent by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold provider startup registers the tool definition. Provider/model prompt caching may reduce repeated token computation after the first request, but the diff supplies eager metadata at launch; no repository cache coalesces schemas across sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed flag and provider mappings are explicit, but first-turn performance is an intentional tradeoff rather than a reportable regression by itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The first-turn net effect may be beneficial because it removes discovery latency; provider-specific prompt encoding and caching determine the exact byte/token cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for the initial turn: eager loading is required by the feature and may reduce first-title latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue or restore an active-agent session after its automatic title has already been settled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The title controller suppresses the rename reminder, but provider launch retains the session's `activeAgent` strategy and the changed definition remains eager. Each subsequent model request therefore carries a model-visible tool that is not needed for automatic naming.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Include the full `rename_chat` schema in the always-loaded model tool set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per later model request for affected Claude and tool-search-enabled Copilot sessions; no new cost for Codex, which was already eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: `deferLoading: true` kept this schema behind provider tool discovery, so ordinary later turns did not eagerly load it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model request serialization/transmission and input processing occur before each response can be generated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of later model turns per active-agent chat, multiplied by concurrently active/restored sessions; the definition contains a long description and four-property schema.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turns are serialized within a chat, so cost repeats sequentially per turn; independent sessions add aggregate concurrent network and model-token load.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted agent/user title metadata prevents another automatic naming reminder, but is not consulted by the new eager-loading branch. Provider prompt caches may discount warm-prefix computation, but do not restore the previous deferred tool state and their effectiveness is provider/model dependent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: title-settled state, immutable strategy, changed flag, and both provider mappings are directly established in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency and token cost depend on provider prompt caching and conversation length; restored and long-lived sessions make the repeated mechanism realistic even though only one tool is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity eager-work regression because the initial-turn requirement is extended to every later turn and already-titled restored sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use utility or deferred title generation, including explicit user-requested rename
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed `activeAgent` branch is not taken. Utility sessions continue to disable `rename_chat`; deferred sessions retain the explicit-only deferred definition and invoke existing persistence only when the user asks to rename.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence sequence per explicit user rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same persistence and deferred tool metadata behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit renames await persistence as before; automatic deferred-title refinement is separate and unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One definition decision per session materialization; explicit rename call count follows user requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency behavior changes; rename persistence follows the existing per-invocation path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, invalidation, or positive/negative cache behavior changes for these strategies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the branch conditions and unchanged deferred transformation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to this diff; these strategy branches preserve prior loading behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression for utility or deferred sessions.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both changed files and traced server-tool materialization through Copilot, Claude, and Codex. One low-severity eager-work issue was submitted: strategy-wide eager loading persists after automatic naming is complete, causing repeated model-boundary schema cost. No concrete regression-fix learning record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
